T: added to certain adjectives and adverbs

s.g: More; used to form the comparative.

ety.text: A combination of a euphonic Proto-Slavic yat (ѣ (jě), inherited from *ě) and -ший (-šij) (itself from Proto-Slavic *-jьjь (“comparative suffix”)). This suffix is used with adjectives that used to have a rising tone in the root syllable in Proto-Slavic, whereas the simpler form -ший (-šij) was used with adjectives that used to have a falling tone in the root syllable in Proto-Slavic; as tone has been lost in Russian, such a rule has become muddier.

s.g: alternative form of -ение (-enije): -tion, -ence, -ance, -ity, etc. (suffix used to form abstract nouns from verbs; added especially to verbs ending in -еть (-etʹ), -ить (-itʹ), and certain other endings, but not -ать (-atʹ))
x: жа́рить (žáritʹ, “to roast, to fry”) + -енье (-enʹje) → жа́ренье (žárenʹje, “roasting, frying”)
прости́ть (prostítʹ, “to forgive, to pardon”) + -е́нье (-énʹje) → проще́нье (proščénʹje, “forgiveness, pardon”)

s.g: antimonide (any compound of antimony with more electropositive elements)

ety.text: Borrowed from Polish butelka, from French bouteille (“bottle”).

ety.text: Reflexive of ры́пать (rýpatʹ, “to spring, to fling (oneself)”), which, in its turn, is from Proto-Slavic *rypati (“to burrow; to tear”). Cognate with Czech rýpat, Polish rypać, Bulgarian ри́пам (rípam).

s.g: to pour out, to pour off, to empty, to drain

ety.text: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic съсловие (sŭslovije), from Proto-Slavic *sъslovьje, itself a calque of Ancient Greek σύγκλητος (súnklētos) / σύλλογος (súllogos). By surface analysis, со- (so-) + сло́во (slóvo) + -ие (-ije).

s.g: to pick, to pluck (flowers or fruits)
to ruin, to destroy, to frustrate, to derange (e.g. a plan, work)
to level, to raze (to the ground), to demolish (a building)
